::: {.layout} ::: {.sidebar} ![](images/profile.jpg){.profile-photo} Postdoctoral Researcher University of Delaware · NSF CHEER Hub *Adaptive decision science for evolving infrastructure and community risk* [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=xpaSPBMAAAAJ&hl=en) [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jingya-wang-purdue/) [wangjy@udel.edu](mailto:wangjy@udel.edu) ::: {.sidebar-section} ### Research Interests - Infrastructure & Community Risk and Resilience - Adaptive Decision-Making under Deep Uncertainty - Climate Adaptation & Multi-Hazard Risk - Stakeholder Dynamics, Land Use & Public Policy - Optimization, Simulation & AI for Decision Support ::: ::: ::: {.main} ## About Me ::: {.highlight-box} Risk and decisions shape each other over time. My research investigates how evolving hazards, the built environment and infrastructure, and stakeholder decisions interact to shape future risk and inform adaptive decision-making under uncertainty. :::

✨ I am on the 2026–2027 academic job market for faculty positions!

I am a Postdoctoral Researcher at the [CHEER Hub](https://www.drc.udel.edu/cheer/) within the University of Delaware's Disaster Research Center, working with [Rachel Davidson](https://ccee.udel.edu/faculty/rachel-davidson/) and [Linda Nozick](https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/people/linda-k-nozick/). My current research uses regional risk simulation and multi-stakeholder modeling to investigate how development, household behavior, insurance, and public policies reshape future risk and the distribution of resilience benefits. I earned my Ph.D. in Industrial Engineering from Purdue University, advised by [David Johnson](https://engineering.purdue.edu/IE/people/ptProfile?resource_id=126281). My doctoral research developed reinforcement learning and optimization-based methods for adaptive flood risk management under deep uncertainty. I also contributed regional flood-risk analyses to Louisiana's $50 billion Coastal Master Plan. I subsequently worked as a Senior Flood Engineer at Karen Clark & Company, contributing to the development of large-scale U.S. flood and hurricane catastrophe models. My work has been recognized through peer-reviewed publications, competitive funding, and professional leadership. I received a $48,448 NSF–Every Page Foundation Ocean Decade Champion award as Principal Investigator and served as Chair of the [Engineering and Infrastructure Specialty Group](https://www.sra.org/risk-analysis-specialty-groups/engineering-and-infrastructure/) of the Society for Risk Analysis. ## News - **Aug 2026:** Our paper, [*An Optimization-Based Approach to Developing Computationally Efficient Long-Term Event-Loss Scenario Ensembles*](https://ascelibrary.org/doi/10.1061/AJRUA6.RUENG-2004), is now available in the *ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems, Part A: Civil Engineering*. - **Jul 2026:** Our paper, [*Direct Policy Search for a Risk-Based Levee Design Framework With Scenario Reduction*](https://doi.org/10.1111/jfr3.70248), was published in the *Journal of Flood Risk Management*, advancing adaptive levee investment strategies under deep uncertainty. - **Aug 2026:** Our paper, [*Coupling Land Use Planning and Multi-Stakeholder Dynamics to Inform Disaster Risk Management: Who Pays for Risk and Who Gains from Intervention?*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106222), is now available in the *International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction*. - **May 2026:** Research spotlight presentation at the NHERI Computational Symposium on computational methods for modeling long-term sequences of hazard losses and their implications for recovery and resilience. - **May 2026:** Our paper, [*Stakeholder Dynamics in Disaster Mitigation Funding: The Roles of Timing, Spatial Scale and Allocation Basis in Policy Design*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijdrr.2026.106120), was published in the *International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction*. - **Dec 2025:** Presented first-authored research at the Society for Risk Analysis Annual Meeting on how land-use planning and multi-stakeholder dynamics shape disaster risk and its distribution. [More updates →](news.qmd) ::: :::
